deep.reconstruction:
This is setup material for Grothendieck's 'tame topology' project. A system M_* = (M_I) is given, where each M_I is a collection of 'tame' subsets of R^I for finite index sets I. This is essentially what model theorists later call a structure on R, in the van den Dries sense. An M_*-tame space X is a set |X| with a tame structure, roughly a set identified with a member of some M_n, up to tame isomorphism. Esp_{M_*} is the category of such spaces, with tame maps as morphisms. There is a forgetful functor X -> |X| to (Ens).

Top of the page: the end of a 'transport de structure' statement. Given X in Esp_{M_*} and a bijection alpha: |X| -> E, there is a unique object Y with |Y| = E and a unique arrow f: X -> Y in Esp_{M_*} lifting alpha. In modern terms, the forgetful functor is an amnestic isofibration: structure can be transported uniquely along bijections.

First Proposition, after visible rewriting. The original draft claimed only products of two objects, and a final object under an axiom (M5) 'R_0 ≠ ∅', i.e. the one-point space R^0 is tame. This was struck and replaced by: Esp_{M_*} has finite limits, and X -> |X| commutes with them. The diagonal marginal remarks that the existence of a final object is equivalent to the property (M5).

Second Proposition, for A in M_I: if R^n ∈ M_n for every n ∈ N*, then R^I ∈ M_I for every finite I. This follows by reindexing along bijections I ≅ {1,...,n}. It motivates replacing the infinite family of conditions by a single axiom, (M0) later renumbered (M5): R ∈ M_1, which with stability under products gives R^I ∈ M_I for all finite I. The marginalia discuss how this formulation interacts with the earlier (M5) and with 'compatibility'.

Purpose: these facts prepare the next page. There R receives a canonical tame structure, every tame space embeds in some R^n, and Grothendieck observes that giving M_* is equivalent to giving a triple (E, R, |.|). Here E is a finitely complete category, |.| is a left-exact functor E -> (Ens), and R is an object into which every object embeds via some R^n. That is a categorical (syntactic-category-like) characterization of a tame or o-minimal-type structure.
errors: No mathematical error, but the page is a draft with visible hesitation. Finite products were first claimed, then generalized to finite limits. Equalizers require M_* to be closed under intersection with diagonals (or under fibre products), which is not stated on this page; presumably it is among the axioms (M1)-(M4) given earlier.
The axiom numbering is unstable: (M5) first denotes 'R_0 ≠ ∅' (a final object exists), then the label (M0)/(M5) is reassigned to 'R ∈ M_1'.
The second Proposition is essentially trivial (reindexing by bijections, plus product stability). The 'implies' in (M0) presupposes stability of M_* under products, which is not shown on this page.

ideas.what: Unique transport of tame structure along bijections of underlying sets
ideas.modern_name: Forgetful functor is an amnestic isofibration (structure transport); concrete category over Set
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bourbaki (transport de structure); standard category theory
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki-style notion, used implicitly throughout EGA/SGA

ideas.what: The category of tame spaces defined by a system M_* of tame subsets of R^n has finite limits, preserved by the forgetful functor; a final object exists iff the point is tame
ideas.modern_name: Category of definable sets of a structure (o-minimal / tame structure) is finitely complete, and the underlying-set functor is left exact
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of o-minimality / model theory (van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal structures, 1998); categorical logic (Makkai-Reyes 1977)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches tame topology only in general terms, without this formalism

ideas.what: Replacing 'R^n ∈ M_n for all n' by the single axiom R ∈ M_1, using closure under finite products indexed by finite sets
ideas.modern_name: The ambient-space axiom of a structure in the sense of van den Dries (R^n definable)
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries; o-minimality axiomatics (Pillay-Steinhorn, Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn, 1980s)

ideas.what: Preparation for the next page's equivalence: tame structure M_* corresponds to (finitely complete category E, left-exact functor to Set, object R generating by embeddings into R^n)
ideas.modern_name: Syntactic/definable category of a structure; reconstruction of a structure from its category of definable sets (categorical logic, conceptual completeness)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Makkai-Reyes (1977), Makkai's conceptual completeness; in o-minimal context, implicit in later 'definable categories' work

missed.claim: The finite-limit and transport-of-structure statements set up an intrinsic, categorical definition of a tame-topology framework: a finitely complete category with a left-exact faithful-type functor to Set and a 'line' object R. This parallels categorical logic's syntactic categories, with R playing the role of the generic sort. The o-minimality literature did not adopt this categorical presentation. The real content is on the next page; this page is only the preparatory lemma.
missed.quote: Dans la catégorie Esp_{M_*} des espaces M_*-modérés, il y a des limites finies et le foncteur X ↦ |X| y commute
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a modest early instance of treating o-minimal / tame structures as categories with a fibre functor. That viewpoint resurfaces in work on definable categories and in attempts to formalize Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée', but its content is largely known to categorical logicians.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine foundational setup (finite limits, transport of structure, simplifying an axiom) for a tame-topology formalism closely matching later o-minimal 'structures'. It is historically interesting as evidence that Grothendieck axiomatized tame sets via systems M_n, but the mathematics here is elementary and known; the more notable categorical equivalence appears on the next page.
transcription_corrections: The subscript on Esp appears to be M_* (or M_•), consistent with the next page, rather than M.
'[?] f : X → Y' is most likely 'flèche f : X → Y'.
The struck parenthetical under 'des espaces' reads roughly '(des deux objets sans transitions)'. It is followed by the struck-through, then reinstated, 'M_*-modérés'.
'(M5) R_0 ≠ ∅' may be 'M_0 ≠ ∅' or 'R^0 ∈ M_0', i.e. the one-point space is tame (existence of the final object).
The diagonal marginal in the middle reads roughly: '...l'existence d'objet final, qui est équivalente à la propriété (M5)...'.
In the second Proposition, the inserted text above is likely '(des A ∈ M_I)'. The condition reads 'Si pour tout n ∈ N* on a R^n ∈ M_n, alors pour tout I fini R^I ∈ M_I'.
The final axiom is labelled first (M0), then relabelled (M5): 'R ∈ M_1 (⇒ ∀ I ∈ (Ens finis), R^I ∈ M_I)'.
